![](images/thomas-baynum.jpg){.headshot fig-alt="Thomas Baynum, smiling, in a navy striped polo shirt against a plain wall."}

Every job I've had came down to making the numbers agree. Route logs and hours of service rules as a CDL Class A driver. Nightly cash and card batches as a restaurant assistant general manager. An average of 800 or more invoices a month as an accountant at a state agency. Now I handle payroll deductions and benefit premiums on a benefits team, and between pay cycles I've built Power BI and Power Query tools that do the matching and show exactly where a variance came from.

I like to know how a system works, not just what it outputs: when the cash arrives, when a change is keyed, when it posts and when each report runs. Most "errors" turn out to be timing, and knowing which is which is the job.

I'm open to **data analyst** roles, with a growing interest in **AI operations and enablement**: anywhere reconciliation, reporting, clean data and the careful use of AI matter.

## Where it started

There was no set process for pulling a year of payroll data together for 401(k) testing. Then I discovered Power Query, and realized it would work if every pay period's file matched: same tables, same sheet names, clean data. So I made them match, then appended and pivoted a full year into one table. That's when I knew I wanted to do this for a living.
